newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends steady, longs nervous.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends steady, longs nervous.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended Monday almost unchanged after an early rally, and brokers said some nervousness was entering the market as mild weather hit Europe and temperatures in the U.S. northeast were normal.
Nov gas oil closed at $234 a tonne, having touched a high of $238 as Brent peaked at $24.75 per barrel. By 1712 GMT, Dec Brent had eased to $24.49.
"The market feels a little tired. A lot of people are sitting on long positions... and it could turn quickly," a broker said.
He said crude and heating oil futures showed a historical tendency to fall sharply between mid-Oct and mid-Nov, and remained nervous of such a fall this year.

Markets had gained some ground over the weekend after oil industry leaders meeting with U.S. Energy Secretary last Friday agreed only limited steps to avert a possible heating oil stock crisis this winter.

Energy Secretary Hazel O'Leary said at least two companies had agreed to take steps to boost output. Citgo said it would delay maintenance to a catalytic cracker and Tosco would maximise refinery output earlier than normal, O'Leary said.
